residencyRequirements.description: Either spouse must have been ordinarily resident in Prince Edward Island for at least one year immediately before the divorce application (Divorce Act, s.3(1)).

waitingPeriod.description: No mandatory waiting period after filing. The 1-year separation must be completed before or by the time the application is granted. Divorce Order effective 31 days after made (Divorce Act, s.12).

noFault.name: One-Year Separation
noFault.description: Spouses have lived separate and apart for at least one year immediately preceding the determination of the divorce application.

fault.name: Physical or Mental Cruelty
fault.description: Respondent has treated applicant with physical or mental cruelty rendering cohabitation intolerable.

terminology.custody: Parenting Time and Decision-Making Responsibility (updated terminology per 2021 Divorce Act amendments; prior terminology: Custody and Access)
terminology.alimony: Maintenance (PEI terminology under the Maintenance Enforcement Act and Family Law Act, RSPEI 1988, c. F-2.1 — not 'spousal support')
terminology.maritalProperty: Matrimonial Property (Matrimonial Property Act, RSPEI 1988, c. M-6)

basic.name: Petition for Divorce
basic.description: Initiates the divorce proceeding in the Supreme Court of Prince Edward Island (Family Section)

basic.name: Divorce Order
basic.description: Draft order to be submitted to court

legalCitations.description: Federal divorce statute — governs divorce proceedings in all provinces and territories

legalCitations.code: Matrimonial Property Act, RSPEI 1988, c. M-6
legalCitations.description: PEI statute — equal division of matrimonial property on marriage breakdown

legalCitations.code: Family Law Act, RSPEI 1988, c. F-2.1
legalCitations.description: PEI statute — spousal and child support, domestic contracts

legalCitations.code: Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act, RSPEI 1988, c. C-33
legalCitations.description: PEI statute — jurisdiction over custody and access orders
Federal guidelines for calculating child support

filingFees.notes: PEI filing fee for a Petition for Divorce is CAD $100 under the Court Fees Act Fees Regulations, plus a $10 Central Registry of Divorce Proceedings fee. Fee waiver may be available for parties who cannot afford the filing fee.

childSupportGuidelines.notes: Federal Child Support Guidelines apply in all provinces

spousalSupportGuidelines.notes: SSAG are advisory only — not legislatively mandated but widely applied by courts

effectiveDateRule: 31 days after the divorce order is made, unless the court varies the effective date or both parties waive the waiting period (Divorce Act, s.12).
certificateNote: A Certificate of Divorce may be obtained from the court office after the effective date of the Divorce Order (Divorce Act, s.12(7)).
notes: Prince Edward Island is the smallest Canadian province by area and population. The Supreme Court of Prince Edward Island (Family Section) handles all divorce matters. Matrimonial property is divided equally by default under the Matrimonial Property Act.
